approaches.title: Refinement proof from cyclic tag systems to Rule 110
approaches.method: Define finite Rule 110 windows with a periodic ether outside, cyclic tag systems, and a decoding relation in Lean 4. Prove a one-step simulation theorem by decomposing each compiled tag step into a finite sequence of glider phases; discharge each collision lemma with a kernel-evaluated finite trace and compose them by induction on tag-system runs.
steps: Formalize Rule 110 evolution on integers and prove locality and light-cone lemmas.
Encode Cook's ether phases, gliders and compiler from cyclic tag words.
Generate every required collision trace and prove its decoded precondition and postcondition by decide.
Prove phase synchronization, noninterference and the global simulation theorem without sorry.
approaches.decisive_result: A compiling Lean module whose theorem maps every finite cyclic-tag execution of length k to a Rule 110 execution decoding the same k transitions, with all collision and ether lemmas proved and only standard axioms.
approaches.failure_signature: A required compiler collision has no finite spacetime trace with Cook's advertised phase and separation constraints, or collision lemmas cannot be composed because debris enters another light cone.
approaches.missing: A machine-readable transcription of Cook's complete glider phase table and substantial Lean proof engineering.

approaches.title: Certified collision-table reconstruction
approaches.method: Independently reconstruct Cook's construction before formalizing it. Enumerate all ether-relative glider phases and pair/triple collisions inside exact light cones, canonicalize traces modulo translation and ether period, and search for a closed macro-transition system implementing the cyclic tag productions. Emit proof certificates containing initial words, horizons and decoded products for Lean replay.
steps: Enumerate minimal periodic-ether defects up to width 80 and classify velocities over 500 steps.
Enumerate phase-separated collisions up to distance 400 and retain stable products.
Model compilation as a constraint problem over collision phases and spacings.
Replay every selected certificate in Lean and compare the reconstructed table with the published construction.
approaches.decisive_result: A closed, independently generated set of certified macro-transitions sufficient for both cyclic-tag productions and all routing operations, with every trace replayed by Lean.
approaches.failure_signature: Exhaustive bounded search finds that at least one required macro-transition has no phase-consistent realization within the stated bounds, leaving no complete emulation certificate.
approaches.missing: Completeness beyond finite phase and spacing bounds would still require a mathematical argument.

approaches.title: Search for periodic-background tag-system compilers
approaches.method: Treat an eventually periodic tape as left period, finite defect and right period. Enumerate periods up to 12 and defects up to 40 cells, then use symbolic execution and counterexample-guided synthesis to seek macro-configurations representing tag symbols and clock phases. Require compositional transitions, not isolated long transients, and certify candidates by exact simulation.
steps: Implement the six-entry machine and symmetry-reduced eventually periodic configurations.
Mine recurring spacetime motifs and infer finite-state macro-boundaries.
Synthesize encodings of a cyclic tag system with bounded phase jitter.
For any candidate, prove finite transition certificates and formulate an induction invariant in Lean.
approaches.decisive_result: A periodic-background compiler with exact certificates for both tag productions, erasure, appending and clock restoration, followed by a Lean simulation theorem.
approaches.failure_signature: No closed macro-transition set survives adversarial compositions of 10,000 random tag steps despite exhaustive periods and defect bounds; this falsifies the searched compiler family, not universality.
approaches.missing: No completeness theorem says universality must use a short periodic background or local tag encoding.

approaches.title: Decidability via bounded crossing sequences
approaches.method: Seek a negative result for eventually periodic tapes. Define crossing sequences at cell boundaries and prove that the 2-state control plus periodic tails forces either bounded crossing complexity or a pumpable translation cycle. A finite quotient of boundary state, tape color and tail phase would then decide halting and exclude conventional universality.
steps: Enumerate local boundary-return types for each left and right tail period up to symbolic period p.
Conjecture a monotone measure or pumping lemma from exhaustive runs up to 10^9 steps.
Formalize crossing sequences and the tail-phase quotient in Lean.
Derive a halting decider if the bounded-crossing lemma is proved.
approaches.decisive_result: A Lean theorem that every eventually periodic input either enters a computably detected cycle or halts, with an explicit computable bound from the finite defect and periods.
approaches.failure_signature: A generated family has unbounded nonrepeating crossing sequences or simulates an unbounded counter, directly refuting the proposed bounded-crossing lemma.
approaches.missing: A viable global invariant; finite experiments cannot establish decidability.

approaches.title: Collision-circuit synthesis for Rule 54
approaches.method: Build a complete phase-resolved catalog of Rule 54 gliders and collisions, then use SAT-based spacetime synthesis to implement a universal cyclic tag system. Each gate must restore a common ether phase and tolerate every symbol context; exact traces become Lean certificates.
steps: Enumerate periodic-domain defects of width at most 60 and classify velocity and phase.
Enumerate binary and ternary collisions over all relative phases.
Synthesize fanout, delay, annihilation and conditional production modules.
Compose modules into tag steps and test at least 100,000 adversarial random steps before Lean certification.
approaches.decisive_result: A finite library of phase-restoring modules that exactly emulates a known universal cyclic tag system, plus checked traces and a compositional simulation invariant.
approaches.failure_signature: The exhaustive glider basis lacks either reliable fanout or conditional production under all contexts, closing this glider-circuit architecture within the declared bounds.
approaches.missing: Failure of one glider architecture would not prove Rule 54 nonuniversal.

approaches.title: Finite-factor obstruction to universality
approaches.method: Search for a symbolic-dynamics obstruction: a finite-state transducer or invariant cone showing every finite perturbation of each Rule 54 periodic domain decomposes into ballistic particles with ultimately periodic interactions. Infer candidate invariants from de Bruijn graphs, then prove closure and an upper bound on crossing-sequence complexity in Lean.
steps: Construct order-k de Bruijn graphs for k through 24 and minimize future-equivalence classes.
Infer conserved additive charges and particle interaction normal forms.
Attempt a finite-defect decomposition and confluence theorem.
If obtained, prove finite-defect prediction decidable and state the exact restricted nonuniversality result.
approaches.decisive_result: A machine-checked theorem that finite perturbations of specified periodic backgrounds have decidable long-term behavior via a finite particle quotient.
approaches.failure_signature: Future-equivalence class counts grow without stabilization and collision products generate unbounded novel defects, defeating the finite-factor premise.
approaches.missing: Even a finite-defect theorem may not cover arbitrary computable initial configurations.

approaches.title: SAT-certified lower bounds on center-column periods
approaches.method: Encode the triangular Rule 30 light cone and the assertion that the center column is eventually p-periodic after preperiod q as SAT. Use incremental solving for all p up to a declared P and q up to Q, produce DRAT certificates for unsatisfiable cases, and verify certificates independently; formalize the reduction from a certificate to the excluded finite period claim.
steps: Generate bit-blasted Rule 30 constraints with shared subformulas.
Exclude every pair p <= 100000 and q <= 100000 using incremental SAT and symmetry reductions.
Check all UNSAT certificates with an independent verifier.
Formalize the constraint semantics and certificate implication in Lean.
approaches.decisive_result: A Lean-checked theorem excluding every eventual period and preperiod in the stated rectangle, exceeding previous certified bounds.
approaches.failure_signature: A satisfying assignment reproduces from the single-cell seed and yields a genuine period; otherwise solver scaling before a novel bound defeats this approach.
approaches.missing: Finite lower bounds do not prove nonperiodicity.

approaches.title: Algebraic dependency and entropy bounds
approaches.method: Exploit left-permutivity to express center bits as Boolean polynomials of boundary variables, then seek a lemma that any eventual center period imposes repeated polynomial identities of increasing degree. Compute algebraic normal forms to identify a monotone leading monomial and formalize the resulting degree or influence lower bound.
steps: Compute exact algebraic normal forms for center bits through n = 4096.
Conjecture and prove a recurrence for a distinguished monomial or discrete derivative.
Show an eventual period would force equality of incompatible derivatives.
Formalize the recurrence and contradiction in Lean.
approaches.decisive_result: A Lean theorem proving non-eventual-periodicity, or a new theorem that center-bit algebraic degree or influence grows unboundedly.
approaches.failure_signature: The proposed distinguished monomial cancels infinitely often or the derivative recurrence admits periodic center sequences, invalidating the invariant.
approaches.missing: A currently unknown invariant connecting global left-permutivity to the single seeded center column.

approaches.title: Quantifier-eliminate all three-node sign patterns
approaches.method: Represent a three-species Jacobian with prescribed zero/sign entries and diagonal diffusion with one to three positive diffusivities. Turing capability is an existential semialgebraic formula: stability at wave number zero plus instability for some q > 0. Use cylindrical algebraic decomposition per sign pattern, then translate compact certificates into determinant, trace and Routh-Hurwitz lemmas checked in Lean.
steps: Canonicalize all 3-node signed directed graphs under permutation and global rescaling.
Write exact Routh-Hurwitz and diffusion-shift inequalities.
Run exact quantifier elimination and extract parameter witnesses or infeasibility certificates.
Prove the classification theorem and check every graph against numerical witnesses.
approaches.decisive_result: Necessary and sufficient conditions for every canonical 3-node sign pattern, with exact rational witnesses for capable classes and checked algebraic contradictions for incapable classes.
approaches.failure_signature: Quantifier elimination cannot finish after decomposition, or numerical capability disagrees with an exact certificate, exposing an encoding error.
approaches.missing: Efficient proof-certificate translation from quantifier elimination into Lean.

approaches.title: Asymptotic capability fraction for random sign graphs
approaches.method: Define an explicit random topology ensemble with independent directed edges, signs and m diffusers. For n = 3 through 8, estimate existence of Turing parameters by global optimization followed by interval verification, stratified by feedback-cycle signatures. Fit finite-size scaling and seek constructive sufficient conditions based on an embedded capable motif plus weak couplings.
steps: Pre-register graph ensemble, parameter box and interval verification criterion.
Enumerate n <= 5 exactly and sample at least 100000 graphs for each larger n and m.
Verify candidate instabilities with interval eigenvalue bounds.
Prove an embedding lemma that preserves instability under sufficiently small added couplings.
approaches.decisive_result: A verified lower bound on the capable fraction with 99% binomial intervals and a theorem showing a stated motif family remains capable for all n.
approaches.failure_signature: Capability fraction remains bounded away from one after conditioning on feedback, or supposed motif extensions lose instability under every admissible coupling.
approaches.missing: Sampling cannot by itself settle the almost-all conjecture.

approaches.title: Lean taxonomy of Hamilton-rule statements
approaches.method: Formalize finite populations as weighted probability spaces and allele-frequency change as a covariance identity. Separate three statements: the Price-equation regression identity, an additive causal fitness theorem with exogenous coefficients, and a frequency-dependent predictive rule. Prove the first two under explicit hypotheses and encode a minimal counterexample to the third.
steps: Define reproductive value, fitness, genotype and social-partner genotype on a finite probability space.
Prove the Price covariance identity and least-squares decomposition including zero-variance cases.
Derive rb > c iff positive allele-frequency change under additive linear fitness and transmission assumptions.
Exhaustively search two- and three-player games for a rational frequency-dependent counterexample and check it in Lean.
approaches.decisive_result: A no-sorry Lean module whose theorem boundaries exactly identify when rb > c is an identity, a predictive theorem, or false, including a checked finite countermodel.
approaches.failure_signature: The proposed countermodel disappears when relatedness and costs are defined consistently, or the predictive theorem needs assumptions equivalent to its conclusion.

approaches.title: Exhaustive finite-population boundary map
approaches.method: Enumerate finite haploid models with population size 2 through 8, binary action, mutation, assortment and all rational payoff tables on a coarse grid. Compute exact one-generation allele change, regression r, b and c, and causal intervention effects. Classify disagreements among identity, additive and causal readings and mine minimal assumption sets with decision trees.
steps: Predefine each Hamilton-rule estimator and degeneracy handling.
Enumerate transition kernels using exact rational arithmetic.
Record minimal models where each reading predicts the wrong sign.
Generalize recurring boundaries into conjectured lemmas for Lean.
approaches.decisive_result: A complete exact atlas for the declared model class, with minimal counterexamples and zero unexplained disagreements between implementation and formal definitions.
approaches.failure_signature: Classification depends primarily on arbitrary regression conventions rather than model structure, preventing a stable scope taxonomy.

approaches.title: Interval-certified cylinder attractors
approaches.method: Fix a smooth finite-range repulsion kernel and reduce the cylindrical placement process to a finite-memory map after proving an exponential tail bound. Use interval Newton and cone conditions to certify fixed or periodic lattice branches, then cover the state space with boxes whose images enter certified basins or declared unresolved sets.
steps: Specify kernel, growth parameter interval and finite-memory truncation error.
Continue Fibonacci, Lucas and bijugate branches with interval arithmetic.
Certify hyperbolicity and trapping neighborhoods.
Run a validated box-cover basin computation and formally check interval certificates.
approaches.decisive_result: For a nontrivial growth interval, a rigorous list of all attractors and basin-volume bounds whose uncovered state-space measure is below 10^-6.
approaches.failure_signature: Persistent positive-measure unresolved boxes or a certified additional attractor outside the proposed branches disproves completeness.
approaches.missing: Validated numerics infrastructure for the model's discontinuous least-repulsion placement rule.

approaches.title: Empirical basin frequencies from randomized primordia
approaches.method: Pre-register a computational experiment over growth parameters and perturbation amplitudes. Sample 100000 initial states per stratum using a declared uniform phase measure, simulate until convergence diagnostics stabilize, classify parastichy pairs, and estimate basin probabilities with simultaneous multinomial confidence intervals. Compare cylinder and disc geometries.
steps: Fix repulsion kernel, numerical precision, initial-state measure and attractor classifier.
Validate convergence classifications against high-precision reruns.
Estimate basin probabilities on an adaptive parameter grid.
Search rare trajectories for unknown attractors and hand them to interval certification.
approaches.decisive_result: A reproducible basin atlas with 99% lower confidence bound above 0.999 for the Fibonacci basin in any claimed small-growth interval, or a measured non-Fibonacci mass exceeding 0.001.
approaches.failure_signature: Classifier instability under precision doubling or discovery of persistent unclassified trajectories above 0.1% prevents the full-measure inference.
approaches.missing: Simulation cannot prove full measure.

approaches.title: Phylogenetic decomposition of diversity constraints
approaches.method: Pre-register a phylogenetic hierarchical model for autosomal synonymous diversity across at least 150 animal species. Predict log diversity from log census proxy, recombination-map length, functional genomic density, body size, range area from GBIF, and generation time, with clade random slopes and measurement error. Compare neutral, linked-selection and boom-bust models by leave-one-clade-out expected log predictive density.
steps: Freeze taxon inclusion, one diversity estimate per species and GBIF coverage rules before fitting.
Require at least 30 species with measured recombination maps and 150 total with range proxies.
Fit matched neutral, background-selection and recurrent-sweep models with a fixed phylogeny.
Report slope residuals, variance explained and held-out calibration.
approaches.decisive_result: Linked selection closes the gap only if its model improves leave-one-clade-out ELPD by at least 10 and leaves an absolute census-diversity slope residual below 0.05; otherwise the residual is quantitatively unresolved.
approaches.failure_signature: Fewer than 30 independent recombination landscapes or posterior predictions dominated by range-size measurement error make the mechanism comparison underpowered.
approaches.missing: Comparable recombination maps and defensible census sizes are sparse outside model organisms.

approaches.title: Genome-window test of linked-selection predictions
approaches.method: Within species, use genome windows to avoid uncertain census sizes. For at least 20 species with polymorphism, recombination and annotation data, preregister the reduction in neutral diversity near conserved or selected sites predicted by background-selection maps, then aggregate the measured maximum genome-wide reduction into a cross-species upper bound on how much linked selection can compress diversity.
steps: Select species and neutral-site filters without inspecting diversity-recombination associations.
Fit a common monotone recombination-diversity model with species-specific intercepts.
Cross-validate chromosome-held-out predictions and estimate diversity absent linked selection.
Regress corrected diversity on GBIF range and life-history proxies.
approaches.decisive_result: If linked selection explains at least 80% of within-genome neutral-diversity variance and corrected cross-species diversity spans under two orders of magnitude, it is sufficient for the tested taxa; a corrected span above three orders refutes sufficiency.
approaches.failure_signature: Neutral-site definitions or recombination maps are incomparable enough that chromosome-held-out prediction R2 is below 0.1 in more than half the species.
approaches.missing: Harmonized population-genomic callsets and recombination maps.

approaches.title: Phylogenetic model comparison across endotherms
approaches.method: Pre-register adult, postabsorptive, thermoneutral basal-metabolism inclusion rules and fit mammal and bird data with phylogenetic generalized least squares. Compare fixed slopes 2/3 and 3/4, an estimated common slope, clade-specific slopes and a quadratic log-mass model using leave-one-family-out prediction.
steps: Resolve taxa against the organisms layer and deduplicate measurements by source.
Require at least 300 species and 20 families, recording temperature and measurement protocol.
Fit all five models with body-temperature and study random effects.
Use family-held-out ELPD and calibrated residuals for the preregistered verdict.
approaches.decisive_result: Universality is supported only if one common-slope model beats every curved or clade-varying model by ELPD at least 10 and its 95% interval width is below 0.04; otherwise report the best heterogeneity structure.
approaches.failure_signature: Protocol covariates are missing for over 30% of records or 2/3 and 3/4 remain inside the common-slope interval, yielding an inconclusive universal exponent.

approaches.title: Formal audit of the WBE exponent derivation
approaches.method: Encode an idealized branching network with branch ratio, length ratio, radius ratio, terminal-unit invariance and space-filling assumptions. Prove each exponent implication separately in Lean, including where area preservation or impedance minimization enters, and construct countermodels when assumptions are weakened.
steps: Represent finite self-similar trees and derive total serviced volume and network volume.
Prove logarithmic exponent lemmas with positivity and nondegeneracy hypotheses.
Derive 3/4 only from a named minimal assumption set.
Use exact finite trees to exhibit assumption-compatible alternatives producing 2/3 or other exponents.
approaches.decisive_result: A no-sorry theorem stating the minimal explicit hypotheses implying exponent 3/4, plus checked countermodels showing which omitted hypotheses destroy the conclusion.
approaches.failure_signature: The biological assumptions cannot be stated without directly assuming the desired scaling relation, showing that the derivation has no independent formal content.
approaches.missing: Formalization settles logical validity, not whether organisms satisfy the assumptions.

approaches.title: Coverage-corrected island model tournament
approaches.method: Select at least 30 oceanic archipelagos and construct standardized GBIF checklists with equal-coverage rarefaction. Fit power law, log-series, Lomolino and METE forms using the same observation model, area covariates and spatially blocked cross-validation. Estimate archipelago-specific z with partial pooling.
steps: Freeze island polygons, taxonomic groups, dates and minimum 1000 occurrences per archipelago.
Estimate completeness from singleton and doubleton frequencies and rarefy to 80% coverage.
Fit all candidate forms with identical detection offsets.
Hold out whole islands and compare predictive log density and z heterogeneity.
approaches.decisive_result: A universal power law requires ELPD at least 10 above every alternative and between-archipelago SD(z) below 0.03 around a mean within 0.03 of 0.25; nonoverlapping z intervals or superior non-power prediction refutes it.
approaches.failure_signature: Coverage estimates below 0.5 for more than one third of archipelagos or severe geographic sampling clustering makes the test inconclusive.
approaches.missing: Reliable island polygons and absence-aware inventories for poorly sampled archipelagos.

approaches.title: Scale-transition test within nested surveys
approaches.method: Use nested quadrat and island inventories to test whether apparent z changes predictably with sampled area. Pre-register local-slope estimators d log S/d log A for power-law and METE curves, and compare them on datasets with at least six nested area scales and 50 species.
steps: Assemble at least 50 independent nested sampling series without pooling nonnested sites.
Estimate local slopes with a monotone spline whose smoothing is fixed by simulation.
Compare constant-slope and METE-predicted slope curves by leave-one-scale-out prediction.
Meta-analyze effects with biome and taxon moderators.
approaches.decisive_result: Scale dependence is supported if at least 70% of series show directional local-slope change and the non-power model improves total ELPD by at least 20; otherwise a constant exponent remains adequate.
approaches.failure_signature: Fewer than 30 series retain six scales after harmonization or richness estimates are dominated by unequal effort.
approaches.missing: A harmonized public collection of genuinely nested surveys.

approaches.title: PBDB subsampled hat-shape census
approaches.method: Query all PBDB marine orders and families with at least 200 occurrences, 20 genera and 10 occupied time bins. Apply shareholder-quorum subsampling at quorum 0.6, align each clade to fractional lifetime, and quantify hat shape by peak interiority and signed monotonicity before and after the peak. Compare against occurrence-preserving time randomizations.
steps: Freeze taxonomy, time scale, quorum and clade thresholds before downloading occurrences.
Run 1000 subsampling replicates per clade.
Generate 10000 null trajectories preserving duration, total occurrences and bin-level sampling intensity.
Control false discovery rate at 0.05 and report the supported fraction with bootstrap intervals.
approaches.decisive_result: Universality requires more than 75% of eligible clades to be significantly hat-shaped and the lower 95% interval above the 95th null percentile; equivalence to the null refutes it.
approaches.failure_signature: Results reverse across reasonable quorum values 0.4 to 0.7 or fewer than 50 clades meet inclusion, indicating sampling dependence.

approaches.title: Birth-death observation-model discrimination
approaches.method: Fit each clade with a state-space birth-death model whose fossil observations have bin-specific sampling probability. Compare constant-rate, diversity-dependent, symmetric hat and asymmetric rise-decline processes by simulation-based calibration and leave-future-bins-out prediction. Include only clades passing posterior identifiability checks.
steps: Simulate 10000 clades per model across PBDB-like sampling regimes to calibrate model recovery.
Specify priors and identifiability thresholds before fitting real clades.
Fit at least 50 eligible clades and evaluate posterior model probabilities.
Repeat with monophyletic clades only and quantify pull-of-the-recent sensitivity.
approaches.decisive_result: A biological hat process is supported if calibrated posterior probability exceeds 0.9 in a majority of identifiable clades and outpredicts sampling-only models; failure to recover simulated hats first invalidates the test.
approaches.failure_signature: Simulation-based calibration confuses hats with sampling heterogeneity in more than 20% of cases, so observed symmetry cannot identify the process.
approaches.missing: Reliable monophyly annotations and computationally intensive state-space inference.

approaches.title: Held-out shell occupancy mechanism tournament
approaches.method: Measure Raup W, D and T from at least 1000 openly digitized adult shells spanning 100 genera with MorphoEval. Fit three preregistered occupancy models: developmental covariance from mantle growth, finite-element failure and stability thresholds, and a phylogenetic diffusion model. Hold out entire families to distinguish interpolation from mechanism.
steps: Blindly validate automated parameters against 100 manual measurements with ICC above 0.9.
Specify feasible regions for each mechanistic model before inspecting occupancy.
Fit models to 80% of families and predict voxel occupancy in held-out families.
Compare proper scoring rules and map false-positive empty regions.
approaches.decisive_result: A mechanism wins if its held-out log score exceeds phylogenetic diffusion by at least 20 and predicts at least 80% of occupied voxels while falsely allowing under 20% of robustly empty voxels.
approaches.failure_signature: Parameter ICC below 0.9 or no model improves family-held-out prediction over phylogenetic diffusion.
approaches.missing: A sufficiently large consistently oriented set of open 3D shell meshes.

approaches.title: Mechanics-derived forbidden-region simulation
approaches.method: Generate shells across a dense W-D-T lattice and simulate growth, self-intersection, center-of-mass stability and pressure loading. Use interval geometry for self-intersection and validated finite-element convergence for failure. Compare the predicted infeasible boundary to observed morphospace without fitting boundary parameters to occupancy.
steps: Evaluate at least one million W-D-T points with adaptive refinement near constraints.
Certify self-intersection and aperture occlusion geometrically.
Compute dimensionless stress and stability under preregistered material ranges.
Test whether observed taxa lie inside the feasible set and empty voxels outside it.
approaches.decisive_result: Functional constraint explains emptiness if at least 90% of observed shells are feasible and at least 70% of well-sampled empty voxels are infeasible across the full material range.
approaches.failure_signature: Large connected empty regions remain mechanically feasible, or more than 10% of observed shells are classified impossible.
approaches.missing: Species-specific shell material properties and loading regimes.

approaches.title: Cross-species clock-ratio prediction test
approaches.method: Pre-register a comparative dataset of every vertebrate species with independently measured segmentation-clock period, somitogenesis duration and final somite count. Predict count as duration divided by period with no fitted slope, propagate measurement error, and use phylogenetic residual analysis. Require at least 15 species spanning fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals.
steps: Define admissible live-imaging measurements and exclude inferred clock periods.
Blindly extract clock, duration and count in duplicate.
Compute posterior predictive intervals from measurement uncertainties only.
Test absolute percentage error and clade-structured bias.
approaches.decisive_result: Clock-and-wavefront count control is supported if at least 80% of species fall within 15% of the parameter-free prediction and phylogenetic residual SD is below 0.1 log units.
approaches.failure_signature: Three or more independently measured species miss by over 30% in the same direction, or fewer than 10 species have all three direct measurements.
approaches.missing: Direct elongation-duration and clock-period measurements exist for too few species.

approaches.title: Clock-wavefront perturbation identifiability map
approaches.method: Build a stochastic delayed-oscillator plus moving-wavefront model and perform global sensitivity analysis over clock period, axis elongation, coupling delay and arrest-front speed. Reproduce published perturbation time courses, then identify perturbations whose somite-count outcomes discriminate period control from elongation control.
steps: Implement a spatial oscillator chain with explicit observation model.
Calibrate separately to each species using only time-course phase and axis length.
Run Sobol sensitivity and profile-likelihood identifiability analyses.
Rank feasible temperature, FGF and Notch perturbations by expected information gain.
approaches.decisive_result: A perturbation is decisive if competing mechanisms predict nonoverlapping 95% intervals separated by at least three somites; publish the top five preregisterable experiments.
approaches.failure_signature: All feasible perturbations have overlapping predictions because period and elongation parameters remain structurally nonidentifiable.
approaches.missing: Executing the discriminating perturbations requires laboratory access.

approaches.title: Errors-in-variables branching exponent test
approaches.method: Analyze at least three independent vascular modalities: retinal images, segmented 3D organ vessels and plant xylem. At each bifurcation fit r_parent^p = r_1^p + r_2^p with hierarchical errors-in-variables likelihood, accounting for pixel resolution, taper and branch-order dependence. Hold out specimens, not branch points.
steps: Pre-register segmentation quality and minimum 500 bifurcations per modality.
Estimate radius uncertainty from repeated segmentation and exclude unresolved vessels.
Fit shared p = 3, p = 7/3, p = 2 and varying-p models.
Compare specimen-held-out predictive density and residual shear dependence.
approaches.decisive_result: General Murray scaling requires p's 95% interval within 0.2 of 3 in every modality and no varying-p model ELPD gain above 10; exclusion of 3 in two modalities refutes generality.
approaches.failure_signature: Radius uncertainty exceeds 20% at most branches or exponent estimates shift by more than 0.3 under preregistered taper corrections.
approaches.missing: Open, quality-controlled 3D vascular trees with calibrated voxel dimensions.

approaches.title: Formal derivation and robust optimality envelope
approaches.method: Formalize Poiseuille pumping cost plus volume-maintenance cost for a bifurcating vessel in Lean. Prove strict convexity, derive the optimal radius-flow relation, and derive the cubic junction law under flow conservation. Then vary the drag exponent and maintenance cost to obtain a theorem mapping physical assumptions to branching exponent.
steps: Define positive radii, flows and cost with explicit viscosity and length hypotheses.
Prove existence and uniqueness of the radius minimizer.
Derive the generalized exponent for resistance proportional to r^-k.
Construct counterexamples with load-bearing or nonlaminar cost terms.
approaches.decisive_result: A no-sorry Lean theorem proving p = 3 exactly under named assumptions and a generalized theorem quantifying how p changes when each assumption changes.
approaches.failure_signature: The optimization requires an unacknowledged flow-radius premise equivalent to the cubic law, making the standard derivation circular.

approaches.title: Degree-matched ontology overlap test
approaches.method: Freeze GO terms for morphogenesis and learning or memory, propagate annotations under a declared relation set, and restrict to experimentally supported human and mouse genes. Test overlap against 100000 permutations matched jointly on total annotation count, publication count, protein-interaction degree and gene length; repeat after removing generic signaling and housekeeping terms.
steps: Timestamp ontology and evidence-code filters before retrieving genes.
Fit propensity scores for membership in each gene set from bias covariates.
Compute matched-null overlap z score, odds ratio and semantic-specificity-weighted overlap.
Repeat for ion-channel and gap-junction genes and across species.
approaches.decisive_result: Wide overlap requires odds ratio at least 2, empirical P below 0.001 and replication in both human and mouse after generic-term removal; an odds ratio between 0.8 and 1.25 supports no enrichment.
approaches.failure_signature: Balance diagnostics retain standardized covariate differences above 0.1 or enrichment disappears under leave-one-ontology-term-out analysis.

approaches.title: Mechanistic-pathway convergence in INDRA
approaches.method: Move beyond gene lists by constructing evidence-weighted INDRA subnetworks connecting curated morphogenesis phenotypes and learning phenotypes. Compare shared causal intermediates and signed paths to degree-preserving, evidence-count-matched network rewires; require statement-level provenance and hold out papers mentioning both domains.
steps: Ground phenotype-associated genes and retain statements with primary evidence.
Remove cross-domain papers to prevent literature leakage.
Compute shared intermediates, signed-path enrichment and pathway conductance.
Run 10000 constrained rewires preserving node degree and statement evidence bins.
approaches.decisive_result: Mechanistic convergence requires at least twofold excess shared intermediates with empirical P below 0.001 and replication after removing all ion-channel genes; null-level paths refute broad convergence.
approaches.failure_signature: The result is driven by fewer than five hubs or by statements from cross-domain review papers.
approaches.missing: INDRA literature coverage and causal direction are uneven across developmental systems.

approaches.title: Held-perturbation Vmem phenotype decoder
approaches.method: Digitize raw or supplementary Vmem images with specimen-level anatomical outcomes from one system only. Register maps to a common coordinate frame, train a spatial decoder on controls and selected perturbation classes, and hold out entire intervention mechanisms so the test measures pattern-based transfer rather than batch recognition.
steps: Require at least 200 specimens, five perturbations and 30 specimens per held-out class.
Freeze normalization, masks and phenotype labels before model training.
Compare Vmem decoder with morphology-at-imaging-time, batch and permuted-map baselines.
Use nested cross-validation grouped by experiment and intervention.
approaches.decisive_result: Predictive mapping requires held-intervention macro-F1 at least 0.75 and at least 0.15 above every baseline, with bootstrap 95% lower bound above 0.6.
approaches.failure_signature: Performance falls to chance when experiments or intervention mechanisms are held out, indicating batch-specific correlation rather than a transferable code.
approaches.missing: Specimen-linked raw Vmem maps and later phenotype labels may not be publicly available at adequate sample size.

approaches.title: Intervention-generalizing bioelectric simulator
approaches.method: Construct a bounded tissue graph with measured channel classes, gap-junction coupling and cell-state transitions. Fit conductances only on control and one perturbation, then predict spatial Vmem and phenotype under unseen channel, gap-junction and pump interventions. Compare mechanistic predictions to a flexible image-only decoder.
steps: Ground intervention targets and signed channel effects through INDRA CoGEx.
Specify prior parameter ranges and identifiability checks.
Calibrate with simulation-based inference on preregistered training interventions.
Predict held-out Vmem maps and anatomical classes without parameter refitting.
approaches.decisive_result: Mechanistic support requires held-intervention Vmem spatial correlation above 0.7 and phenotype accuracy above 0.75 for at least three distinct intervention classes.
approaches.failure_signature: No single posterior parameter region predicts both Vmem and anatomy, or image-only prediction strongly outperforms simulation on held interventions.
approaches.missing: Quantitative conductance, coupling and longitudinal imaging data for the same specimens.

approaches.title: Matched random-network memory enrichment test
approaches.method: Reimplement the exact stimulation and memory criteria for all 35 biological ODE models, then generate 100 matched nulls per model preserving node count, signed degree sequence, kinetic-law family, parameter marginal distributions and stiffness. Blindly apply identical protocols and estimate enrichment with a model-paired conditional logistic regression.
steps: Freeze executable model versions and numerical tolerances.
Validate protocol reproduction against all reported memory calls.
Generate at least 3500 convergent null networks with fixed seeds.
Classify memory, habituation and consolidation using preregistered effect thresholds.
approaches.decisive_result: Biological enrichment requires paired odds ratio at least 2 with 99% interval excluding 1 for a memory class and replication across two null generators; odds ratio at or below 1 refutes enrichment.
approaches.failure_signature: Fewer than 80% of published calls reproduce or null convergence filtering changes network dynamics enough to break covariate balance.

approaches.title: Dynamical motif attribution of memory
approaches.method: Identify whether memory enrichment is explained by specific feedback motifs rather than biological origin. Enumerate signed three- and four-node motifs, sample kinetic parameters by Latin hypercube, and estimate each motif's memory probability. Decompose each BioModels network's prediction with motif counts and targeted edge ablations.
steps: Enumerate nonisomorphic signed motifs with self-loops handled explicitly.
Run at least 10000 parameter sets per motif under the fixed memory protocol.
Fit a sparse hierarchical predictor from motif content to memory behavior.
Ablate predicted motifs in biological models and matched nulls.
approaches.decisive_result: A motif mechanism is established if its presence increases memory probability by at least 0.25 and deleting it abolishes memory in at least 80% of predicted biological models while matched control deletions do not.
approaches.failure_signature: Memory depends on diffuse parameter combinations and no motif has stable effects across kinetic families.
approaches.missing: Combinatorial parameter sweeps are expensive and motif effects may be context-dependent.

approaches.title: Frozen generative model predicts regeneration times
approaches.method: Choose one planarian regeneration series and fit a fixed generative model only to intact anatomy and unperturbed regeneration. Define sensory states, latent target morphology, likelihood variance and action dynamics before examining graded perturbations. Predict median regeneration time and failure probability as functions of initial variational surprise.
steps: Publish the full generative model, priors and fitting data split before testing.
Compute surprise from initial fragment geometry and Vmem summaries.
Derive posterior predictive time and error curves for held-out perturbations.
Compare against size-only and flexible survival-model baselines.
approaches.decisive_result: The fixed model passes if at least 80% of held-out median times lie within its 90% intervals and surprise improves leave-intervention-out ELPD by at least 10; failure of interval coverage below 50% refutes this instantiation.
approaches.failure_signature: Predictions require changing likelihoods, priors or target morphology after observing each perturbation, demonstrating post hoc flexibility.
approaches.missing: Open specimen-level regeneration time courses with quantified initial perturbations.

approaches.title: Identifiability and universal-fit stress test
approaches.method: Test falsifiability directly. Generate synthetic morphogenetic trajectories from reaction-diffusion, mechanical relaxation and random state-space models, then fit the same bounded active-inference model class without changing its latent dimension or priors. Estimate how often it fits non-active-inference processes as well as genuine ones.
steps: Predefine model class, parameter bounds and predictive scoring rule.
Generate 1000 datasets per mechanism over matched noise and sample sizes.
Fit blindly and perform simulation-based calibration.
Compute specificity, power and parameter identifiability for labeling active inference.
approaches.decisive_result: The framework is discriminative only if power and specificity both exceed 0.8 on held-out trajectories; specificity below 0.6 shows the tested formulation can absorb unrelated dynamics.
approaches.failure_signature: Equivalent predictive scores occur across all generators or posterior parameters are nonidentifiable, making empirical attribution unsupported.

approaches.title: Curvature-blinded scutoid frequency test
approaches.method: Segment at least 30 epithelial volumes spanning curvature and thickness, with at least 200 cells each. Before inspecting topology, predict scutoid frequency from a vertex-model energy minimized at measured curvature, cell-number mismatch and apicobasal tension ratio. Test predictions on held-out tissues and compare to topology-preserving random rearrangements.
steps: Validate segmentation topology against manually annotated cells with F1 above 0.95.
Freeze energy parameters using flat epithelia only.
Predict per-volume scutoid fraction and spatial localization.
Compare absolute error and likelihood to random and curvature-only baselines.
approaches.decisive_result: Energy minimization is supported if held-tissue scutoid-frequency error is below 0.1 and at least 50% lower than both baselines, with correct localization in 80% of volumes.
approaches.failure_signature: Predicted frequency is systematically wrong by more than 0.2 or segmentation uncertainty changes scutoid calls by over 10%.
approaches.missing: Enough open volumetric epithelia with diverse measured curvatures.

approaches.title: Certified local optimality of Weaire-Phelan
approaches.method: Restrict the mathematical problem to periodic partitions with fixed Weaire-Phelan combinatorics and finite-dimensional face perturbations. Compute the second variation of area under volume constraints, quotient translation and gauge modes, and certify positive definiteness with interval arithmetic; formalize the constrained Hessian argument in Lean.
steps: Specify a finite periodic fundamental cell and exact constraint manifold.
Derive first- and second-variation formulas symbolically.
Bound geometric coefficients and Hessian eigenvalues by intervals.
Check a Lean theorem converting the certificate to strict local minimality in the restricted class.
approaches.decisive_result: A checked positive lower bound on the constrained Hessian after all symmetry zero modes are removed, proving strict local optimality for the declared perturbation class.
approaches.failure_signature: A certified negative mode gives an explicit area-lowering perturbation, disproving local optimality in that class.
approaches.missing: A tractable exact representation of curved interfaces and a bridge from finite perturbations to arbitrary variations.

approaches.title: Leakage-proof ZFIN discrepancy classifier
approaches.method: Construct gene-level labels only where mutant and morpholino experiments test matched developmental stages and phenotypes. Predict discrepancy using paralog sequence similarity, NMD susceptibility, duplicate age, baseline expression, INDRA network redundancy and annotation counts. Hold out entire paralog families and publication years to prevent near-gene and literature leakage.
steps: Double-label records and require adjudicated agreement above kappa 0.8.
Freeze positive, negative and uncertain definitions before feature extraction.
Require at least 100 positives and 100 matched negatives.
Compare calibrated gradient boosting with logistic and prevalence baselines in nested group cross-validation.
approaches.decisive_result: Predictability requires family-held-out AUROC at least 0.75, AUPRC at least twice prevalence and calibration slope between 0.8 and 1.2; bootstrap lower bounds must exceed baselines.
approaches.failure_signature: Performance collapses below AUROC 0.6 under family or temporal holdout, showing apparent prediction was leakage or annotation bias.
approaches.missing: A clean matched ZFIN label set; phenotype ontology mappings and negative labels require manual curation.

approaches.title: Mechanistic compensation score from decay and paralogs
approaches.method: Build an interpretable score from predicted premature termination and NMD, mutant-transcript abundance, sequence similarity to expressed paralogs, and signed compensatory paths in INDRA. Evaluate the prespecified score without learned weights, then use causal mediation on datasets containing mutant RNA-seq to test whether paralog upregulation mediates phenotype absence.
steps: Define the score and thresholds before joining phenotype labels.
Select at least 50 mutants with RNA-seq, matched knockdown phenotype and paralog information.
Test score discrimination and paralog-expression mediation with bootstrap uncertainty.
Rank untested genes only after the held-out threshold is met.
approaches.decisive_result: Mechanistic support requires odds ratio at least 2 per score SD, AUROC above 0.7 and a positive mediated fraction above 0.3 with 95% interval excluding zero.
approaches.failure_signature: NMD and paralog induction do not precede phenotype rescue, mediation is null, or discrimination is at chance.
approaches.missing: Public mutant RNA-seq paired to rigorously matched morphant and mutant phenotypes.
